knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Scorched wiring inside a controller is an electrical fault. The crew does not open or alter it, records the condition from outside and refers it to a licensed electrician.
A service report describes what was tested, what was found, what was changed and what was referred. It does not present only positive results or claim the system is leak-free.
The backflow prevention device stops water from flowing back from the garden into the supply, which protects drinking water.

practicalCriteria: Given a mock system drawing and a mock zone layout, the learner names the supply point, backflow device, filter, regulator, controller, valves and zones within the assessor's set time.
On a supplied test rig or mock zone, the learner runs each zone with the controller's test function and records coverage and any blocked emitter.
Given a supplied mock supply-side leak, the learner stops, marks the area and states the referral step without opening the device.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Labelled component list for the mock system, signed by the assessor.
Zone run record for the supplied rig, with the assessor's observation.
Referral record for the mock supply-side leak.
stopWorkCriteria: Opening the mock controller enclosure or touching mock mains wiring during the assessment.
Opening or adjusting the mock backflow device during the assessment.
Running a mock zone with a visibly damaged mock valve or open mock wire.
